name: Brachydactyly Type A7

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Brachydactyly Type A7

criteria.description: Presence of shortened or absent middle phalanges of the fingers, especially the fifth digit
Shortening of distal phalanges of the fingers
Radiographic evidence of hypoplasia or aplasia of middle and distal phalanges
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Lack of associated systemic malformations or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of shortened or absent middle phalanges confirmed radiographically in at least one finger, with or without family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may be used if available.

common.symptomName: Aplasia/Hypoplasia of the middle phalanges of the hand

occasional.symptomName: Triangular epiphysis of the middle phalanx of the 2nd finger
Broad distal phalanx of the thumb
Short middle phalanx of the 5th toe

imaging: Radiographs showing hypoplasia or aplasia of middle and distal phalanges
Possible mild carpal bone anomalies on hand X-ray
genetic: Mutations in genes associated with phalangeal development (specific gene not well characterized)
other: Clinical examination revealing shortened fingers with normal skin and nails

distinguishingFeatures: Shortening primarily of middle phalanges of index, middle, and ring fingers
Different pattern of digit involvement compared to BDA7
Shortening of middle phalanges with involvement of metacarpals
Presence of hyperphalangy and other skeletal anomalies
Often associated with systemic diseases or environmental exposures

redFlags: Presence of systemic malformations or syndromic features
references: Temtamy SA, McKusick VA. The Genetics of Hand Malformations. 1978.
